source_text: Oportet quidem nihil post primum opus, quod ad sanctum Turbantium edidi, super necessario naturalium pudore disserere; quia ibi ita plene actum est, ut nisi depositis omnino mentibus, nihil hinc possit ambiguitatis oboriri.
pass_a_gloss: It is fitting indeed after the first work, which I published to holy Turbantius, to discuss nothing further upon the necessary modesty of natural things; because there it was so fully treated that unless minds have been altogether laid down, nothing of ambiguity can arise from here.

lemmas.lexica: LS necessitas; Blaise vs free choice
LS naturalis; Blaise malum naturale=evil as a nature
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS opus; Blaise God's works vs devil's

pass_b_english: After my first work, published to the holy Turbantius, there should be no need to discuss the necessary modesty surrounding natural functions. The matter was handled there so fully that no uncertainty about it can arise unless people abandon their minds altogether.

choices.why: Julian's Manichaean charge: an evil that is a nature, not a will's act.
Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
Julian contrasts opportunity/help with imposed necessity; load-bearing against natural compulsion to sin.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
